---
title: "Seasonal stage x Bd modeling, all species"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: one model form, fit separately to every species with both life stages, describing how
the subadult - adult difference in *Bd* infection changes through the season. The goal is not a
cross-species claim but comparable per-species profiles (e.g. *R. muscosa* vs *R. sierrae*,
*A. canorus* vs *A. americanus* / *A. fowleri*) that can inform what drives susceptibility or
resilience.

How this differs from `02_season_modeling.qmd` (six data-rich species, a separate seasonal curve
per stage):

- **The stage difference is modeled directly**, as a shrinkage difference smooth. When the data
  cannot support a changing difference (narrow or no co-sampling), the smooth shrinks to zero
  and the difference becomes a constant offset. With broad co-sampling, it can bend. So every
  species can use the same model, and the amount of seasonal pattern is learned per species.
- **The season axis starts at each species' seasonal origin** (the middle of its longest
  sampling gap, from `01_season_screen.Rmd`), so each species' sampled season is continuous,
  including Panamanian species whose season straddles the new year.
- **Species list, order and origins come from `01_season_species_all.csv`**, written by the
  screen (all species with >= 20 swabs of each stage).

The six-species stage-curve models remain as a robustness comparison: where both agree, the
pattern does not depend on the parameterization.

Production fits run on the cluster with `r-brms-contained/size_bd_season_all_modeling.R` (same
data prep, formula, priors and settings; `hpc/run_size_bd_season_all_modeling.sbatch`, one species
per array task). Keep the two in sync.

Run order: `size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd` (model data), then the coverage sections of
`01_season_screen.Rmd` (species list).

# Setup

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr, patchwork)

models_dir = here("size_bd_season", "models_all")
dir.create(models_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

# model checks shared across the seasonal models
source(here("size_bd_season", "season_check_functions.R"))

```

# Data
```{r}
# species, cluster array index, seasonal origin and coverage classes from the screen
season_species_all = read_csv(here("size_bd_season", "intermediates", "01_season_species_all.csv"),
                              show_col_types = FALSE)

season_species_all

# season covariate: months since the species' seasonal origin (origin_doy, mid-week of the
# origin week). %% 365 wraps dates before the origin to the end of the axis, so the sampled
# season runs continuously from ~0 to ~12 (in practice a smaller sampled block within that).
# no centering is needed: with shrinkage smooths there is no separate linear slope whose prior
# depends on the units.
#
# stage_o: an ORDERED copy of life stage. a smooth with by = <ordered factor> is built only for
# the non-reference level (subadult), as a deviation from the shared smooth: the difference
# curve. (with an unordered factor, brms / mgcv would build one full curve per level, as in
# 02_season_modeling.qmd.)
prep_season_all_data = function(brms_data, species_name, origin_doy) {
  brms_data %>%
    filter(taxon_capture == species_name) %>%
    mutate(life_stage_simple = factor(life_stage_simple, levels = c("adult", "subadult")),
           stage_o = ordered(life_stage_simple, levels = c("adult", "subadult")),
           doy = as.integer(format(date, "%j")),
           season_m = ((doy - origin_doy) %% 365) / 30.44) %>%
    # drop unused levels so random-effect terms have no empty columns
    droplevels()
}

season_data = season_species_all %>%
  { set_names(.$origin_doy, .$taxon_capture) } %>%
  imap(~ prep_season_all_data(brms_data, .y, .x))

# check: the sampled season should be one block on the new axis (no swabs near both 0 and 12
# unless the species is sampled year-round)
map_dfr(season_data, ~ tibble(n = nrow(.x),
                               season_m_min = min(.x$season_m),
                               season_m_max = max(.x$season_m)),
        .id = "taxon_capture")

```

# Model structure
```{r}

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

# for both the load part (mu, log scale, Bd-positive swabs) and the detection part (hu, logit
# scale of non-detection):
#   1 + life_stage_simple            stage intercepts (adult reference). the subadult coefficient
#                                    is the stage difference where the difference curve is 0;
#                                    if the difference smooth shrinks away, it is THE difference
#   s(season_m, bs = "ts", k = 5)    seasonal curve shared by both stages (adult curve)
#   s(season_m, by = stage_o, bs = "ts", k = 5)
#                                    subadult - adult difference curve, centered (averages ~0
#                                    over the data), so the constant part stays with
#                                    life_stage_simple
#   (1 | population:life_stage_simple), (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year)
#                                    random effects as in the unified / gam / stage-curve models
# sigma ~ 1 + (1 | population)       residual spread of log load varies by population
#
# bs = "ts": shrinkage thin-plate spline. a standard thin-plate spline ("tp") splits into a
# penalized wiggly part and an unpenalized straight line (in brms, a fixed "bs_" slope). "ts"
# adds a small penalty to the straight line too, so ALL of the smooth sits under one sds and the
# whole curve, slope included, can shrink to flat. this is what lets narrow-coverage species
# fall back to a constant stage difference.
season_all_formula = bf(
  bd_load_co100_density ~ 1 + life_stage_simple +
    s(season_m, bs = "ts", k = 5) +
    s(season_m, by = stage_o, bs = "ts", k = 5) +
    (1 | population:life_stage_simple) +
    (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year),

  hu ~ 1 + life_stage_simple +
    s(season_m, bs = "ts", k = 5) +
    s(season_m, by = stage_o, bs = "ts", k = 5) +
    (1 | population:life_stage_simple) +
    (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year),

  sigma ~ 1 + (1 | population)
)

# priors. same scales as the stage-curve models, except the smooth sds:
#   shared smooth sds      student_t(3, 0, 2.5): moderately regularizing, as before
#   difference smooth sds  student_t(3, 0, 1): tighter, so the default is a constant stage
#                          difference and a changing difference must be earned from the data.
#                          the sds is not directly the curve's amplitude (it scales penalized
#                          basis coefficients), so check what it implies with the sds
#                          posterior-vs-prior plot below and adjust if it over- or under-shrinks
# coef names are the smooth terms as brms labels them (copied from default_prior).
sds_shared = 's(season_m, bs = "ts", k = 5)'
sds_diff = 's(season_m, by = stage_o, bs = "ts", k = 5)'

season_all_priors = c(
  # mu: log load density among positives
  prior(normal(5, 4), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 3), class = "b"),                                  # subadult offset
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 2.5)", class = "sds", coef = sds_shared),
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 1)", class = "sds", coef = sds_diff),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),

  # hu: logit of non-detection
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "Intercept", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", dpar = "hu"),                     # subadult offset
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 2.5)", class = "sds", coef = sds_shared, dpar = "hu"),
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 1)", class = "sds", coef = sds_diff, dpar = "hu"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "hu"),

  # sigma: log residual sd of log load
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept", dpar = "sigma"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "sigma")
)

# validate_prior errors if a prior matches no parameter. run for every species: this also
# confirms each species' data can build the smooths (k = 5 needs enough distinct season values)
# and random effects. fast (no sampling).
# expected warning (2 per species, harmless): "the global prior 'student_t(3, 0, 2.5)' of class
# 'sds' will not be used". that is brms' default class-wide sds prior; both smooths have their
# own priors above, so the default has nothing left to apply to.
prior_ok = imap_lgl(season_data, function(d, spp) {
  tryCatch({
    validate_prior(season_all_priors, formula = season_all_formula, data = d,
                   family = hurdle_lognormal())
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(spp, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
    FALSE
  })
})

prior_ok[!prior_ok]   # empty = all species OK

# full prior set for one species (ours plus brms defaults, e.g. lkj on the stage correlation)
validate_prior(season_all_priors, formula = season_all_formula,
               data = season_data[["anaxyrus_canorus"]], family = hurdle_lognormal())

```

# Local timing test
```{r}
#| eval: false

# short run to estimate cluster time for this model form (see 02_season_modeling.qmd for the
# extrapolation logic: warmup x 2000/300, sampling x 2000/100, slowest chain). run at 0.95;
# production uses 0.99 for all but r. sierrae (~1.5-2x slower, see the fitting chunk). three species
# spanning the range of n and population counts:
#   silverstoneia_flotator    n ~600, 17 populations
#   rana_catesbeiana          n ~1.8k, 28 populations
#   notophthalmus_viridescens n ~5.3k, 281 populations (many random-effect levels)
timing_species = c("silverstoneia_flotator", "rana_catesbeiana", "notophthalmus_viridescens")

timing_results = map_dfr(timing_species, function(spp) {
  start = Sys.time()
  fit = brm(
    formula = season_all_formula,
    data = season_data[[spp]],
    family = hurdle_lognormal(),
    prior = season_all_priors,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
    chains = 4, iter = 400, warmup = 300,
    seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
    refresh = 0
  )
  elapsed = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "mins"))
  chain_times = rstan::get_elapsed_time(fit$fit)

  tibble(taxon_capture = spp,
         n = nrow(season_data[[spp]]),
         total_min = elapsed,                                 # includes compilation (~1 min)
         max_chain_warmup_s = max(chain_times[, "warmup"]),
         max_chain_sample_s = max(chain_times[, "sample"]),
         est_production_h = (max(chain_times[, "warmup"]) * 2000 / 300 +
                               max(chain_times[, "sample"]) * 2000 / 100) / 3600,
         divergences = sum(nuts_params(fit) %>% filter(Parameter == "divergent__") %>% pull(Value)))
})

timing_results

```

# Model fitting
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show model fitting code"

# production fits run on the cluster (r-brms-contained/hpc/run_size_bd_season_all_modeling.sbatch).
# this local version is for reference or a single small species.

# sampler target acceptance rate per species, as used on the cluster (ADAPT_DELTA). 0.99 by
# default: the local timing test (at 0.95) showed divergences in small / sparse species, and a
# higher target makes the sampler take smaller steps through tight curvature. this changes how
# the posterior is explored, not the model, so fits at different targets are comparable.
# r. sierrae: 0.95 (well informed; 0.99 would roughly double a ~13-15 h run). record any
# resubmission at a different target here so the code says what each fit used.
season_adapt_delta = function(spp) {
  if (spp == "rana_sierrae") 0.95 else 0.99
}

fit_season_all_model = function(spp) {
  fit = brm(
    formula = season_all_formula,
    data = season_data[[spp]],
    family = hurdle_lognormal(),
    prior = season_all_priors,
    control = list(adapt_delta = season_adapt_delta(spp), max_treedepth = 12),
    chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000,
    seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr"
  )

  fit = add_criterion(fit, "loo")
  saveRDS(fit, file.path(models_dir, paste0("size_bd_season_all_model_zln_d1_", spp, ".rds")))
  fit
}

# e.g. fit_season_all_model("silverstoneia_flotator")

```

# Load fitted models
```{r}
#| eval: false

# cluster fits are copied into size_bd_season/models_all/ (named as in fit_season_all_model).
# species without a fit file yet are skipped with a message.
model_files = file.path(models_dir, paste0("size_bd_season_all_model_zln_d1_",
                                           season_species_all$taxon_capture, ".rds"))
names(model_files) = season_species_all$taxon_capture

missing_fits = names(model_files)[!file.exists(model_files)]
if (length(missing_fits) > 0) message("no fit yet: ", paste(missing_fits, collapse = ", "))

season_models = purrr::map(model_files[file.exists(model_files)], readRDS)

```

# Model checks

Same order as in `02_season_modeling.qmd`: sampler -> predictive fit -> priors. Functions are in
`season_check_functions.R`. With many small species, expect the small ones to be the most
fragile (few populations, few swabs per population-year).

## Convergence
```{r}
#| eval: false

convergence = map_dfr(season_models, conv_check, .id = "taxon_capture") %>%
  left_join(season_species_all %>% select(taxon_capture, coverage_class_prev, coverage_class_load),
            by = "taxon_capture")

convergence

# species needing attention (thresholds as in the comments of conv_check)
convergence %>%
  filter(max_rhat > 1.01 | min_ess_bulk < 400 | min_ess_tail < 400 |
           n_divergent > 0 | min_ebfmi < 0.3)

```

## Smooth sds: posterior vs prior
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| fig-height: 14
#| fig-width: 12

# the difference-smooth sds is the key quantity here: pulled to ~0 = constant stage difference
# (no seasonal change, or data can't tell); well away from 0 and narrower than the prior = the
# data support a changing difference. compare against the coverage class: broad-coverage
# species should be the ones with informative difference sds.
sds_prior = tribble(
  ~smooth,      ~prior_median,              ~prior_upper_95,
  "shared",     half_t_quantile(0.5, 2.5),  half_t_quantile(0.95, 2.5),
  "difference", half_t_quantile(0.5, 1),    half_t_quantile(0.95, 1))

sds_all = map_dfr(season_models, sds_summary, .id = "taxon_capture") %>%
  left_join(season_species_all %>% select(taxon_capture, coverage_class_prev, coverage_class_load),
            by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(coverage_class = if_else(part == "hu", coverage_class_prev, coverage_class_load))

sds_all %>%
  filter(smooth == "difference") %>%
  select(taxon_capture, part, coverage_class, Q2.5, Q50, Q97.5) %>%
  arrange(part, coverage_class, desc(Q50))

sds_all %>%
  left_join(sds_prior, by = "smooth") %>%
  mutate(species = str_to_sentence(gsub("_", " ", taxon_capture)),
         part = if_else(part == "hu", "detection (hu)", "load (mu)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Q50, xmin = Q2.5, xmax = Q97.5, y = species, color = coverage_class)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 0, xmax = prior_upper_95, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey92", color = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = prior_median), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(size = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(part ~ smooth, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "sds (posterior median, 95% interval)", y = NULL, color = "coverage",
       subtitle = "grey band = prior 95% range; dashed = prior median") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"))

```

## Prior sensitivity
```{r}
#| eval: false

# power-scaling sensitivity for the parameters that shape the stage contrast: subadult offsets
# and smooth sds. "prior" > ~0.05 flags a prior-dominated parameter. for the difference sds
# in narrow / none species, prior sensitivity is EXPECTED (that is the shrinkage working); it
# matters for broad-coverage species.
library(priorsense)

season_all_sensitivity = imap(season_models, function(fit, spp) {
  vars = grep("^b_(hu_)?life_stage_simplesubadult$|^sds_", variables(fit), value = TRUE)
  powerscale_sensitivity(fit, variable = vars) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(taxon_capture = spp)
}) %>%
  list_rbind()

season_all_sensitivity %>%
  filter(diagnosis != "-")

```
